02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Arithmetic me.quote: For sequence length N and head dimension d, the paper states that FlashAttention uses O(N squared times d) arithmetic and O(N) additional memory beyond its inputs and output. For on-chip memory size M between d and N times d, its analyzed high-bandwidth-memory accesses are proportional to N squared times d squared divided by M. These bounds describe arithmetic, auxiliary storage, and memory traffic separately.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Backward reco.rationale: Needed partial answer or concrete qualification: Explains extra backward recomputation avoiding large intermediate memory transfers.
02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Backward reco.quote: FlashAttention stores the attention output and row-level softmax statistics instead of retaining the full intermediate score and probability matrices for backward computation. It reconstructs the needed blocks from queries, keys, and values in on-chip memory. The paper describes this as selective gradient checkpointing. In its measured implementation, the additional arithmetic reduces memory accesses enough to make backward computation faster.

02-Zettelkasten/Literature/Blockwise sof.rationale: Needed partial answer or concrete qualification: Blockwise accumulation preserves the attention expression while avoiding full intermediates.

The paper proves that this procedure returns the same attention expression as the full matrix computation.

Evaluating these dimensions separately makes grounded-answer quality more precise and prevents a high citation count from substituting for evidence verification.

A citation assessment should examine whether the set supports the statement and whether each member contributes, reflecting the distinction between coverage and precision.
